The Student Budget Blueprint

Getting the Best Specs for Under $600
Computer Architecture · Course Report
Scroll to open the laptop ↓
CPU

CPU

The brain of the laptop. It runs every instruction your programs give it and coordinates all the other parts. More cores and a higher clock speed mean more work done at once.

For students: a modern Ryzen 5 or Core i5 class chip handles coding, documents and multitasking.
RAM

RAM

Short-term memory. It keeps the apps and files you are using right now within instant reach, so switching between a browser, an IDE and a PDF stays smooth.

For students: 16 GB is the comfortable target. Check whether it is soldered, because then it can never be upgraded.
SSD

SSD

Long-term storage with no moving parts. It holds the system and your files, and it decides how fast the laptop boots and opens programs.

For students: 512 GB gives room for software, projects and course material.
GPU

GPU

The graphics processor. It draws what you see and speeds up 3D, video and CAD. Integrated GPUs share the CPU chip; dedicated ones have their own power.

For students: integrated is enough for study. Choose a Quadro or RTX card only for heavy CAD or 3D.
Battery

Battery

Stores the energy that lets you work away from a socket. Capacity is measured in watt-hours (Wh), and the screen and CPU drain it the most.

For students: check the Wh rating. On refurbished units, battery wear matters most.
Display

Display

The screen you stare at for hours. Size, resolution and panel quality decide how much fits on screen and how comfortable it is on the eyes.

For students: 15.6 to 16 inches at Full HD (1920×1080) is the practical sweet spot.

Three student-friendly directions under $600

Same laptop, three builds. Scroll to take each one apart and see what you actually get.

Acer Aspire 3 (A315-24P)

Approx. US reference price: $590–$600

Best for

Study, browsing, coding and light engineering tasks.

Caution

RAM may be soldered; the integrated GPU is entry-level.

ASUS Vivobook 16 M1605

Approx. US reference price: up to $599 for a listed configuration

Best for

Coursework, documents, programming and multitasking.

Caution

Verify the exact CPU and RAM. Some listings have only 8 GB.

Refurbished Mobile Workstation

Target budget: roughly $400–$600, depending on condition and market

Best for

Heavier CAD and 3D work at lower cost.

Caution

Battery wear, warranty and GPU generation matter. Inspect before buying.

The blueprint in one line

Modern 6-core-class CPU 16 GB RAM 512 GB SSD Full HD display

Spend on the CPU, RAM and SSD first. Add a dedicated GPU only if your coursework needs CAD or 3D.

Prices are US-market reference points and can change. They may not reflect Iraqi retail prices, import fees or availability.
